account:
It is day 1, shortly after eight, and my office appointment is due. I have a grain inspection at the mill at ten, council letters this afternoon, and tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at three. The builder has delivered his signed visual bridge report and explicitly acknowledged receiving the agreed two emeralds. He found the crossing passable, recommended no particular repair, and did not certify structural safety. He is now asking about further work, with scope and price to be agreed first. That looks like ordinary business, not evidence of a hidden undertaking.

The secretary has been managing the records and appointments. The baker came to the hall this morning, but I did not make out his words. The secretary's reply suggests he was seeking a bread order: she said none was authorized and that we would contact him if needed. He has since moved toward the market stall. Yesterday the innkeeper asked for advance notice of visitors or gatherings needing food or lodging, to avoid wasting bread. Those food-related approaches could simply be merchants planning their supplies; I have not heard of any actual gathering or order that connects them.

I still have a feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but the observations presently available do not establish a secret event or who might be organizing one. Several nearby conversations were indistinct, and I should not treat unheard words as evidence. My next priorities are to conduct office business with the secretary, ask about new correspondence or requests, and keep the mill appointment. Those conversations may clarify whether there is any unusual activity beyond routine town business.
